text:
Emma Carter: Quick thread to align on public/social comms for the API latency incident. We need a short tweet, a blog blurb (if needed), and the exact status page wording. Who can take ownership of drafts and who must sign off?

Rajesh Patel: I'm on call and still routing. Root cause looks like a KV cache saturation on the inference runtime — mitigation in progress (scaling + cache bump). We should avoid definitive ETA in public posts.

Lia Gomez: Agree with Rajesh. From infra side we expect partial recovery in 20-40m but can't promise. Status page should say "degraded performance for some requests" not full outage.

SRE-Bot: Incident declared • INC-2026-117 • Severity: Sev2 
SRE-Bot: Current status: Investigating -> Identified (KV cache saturation).

Paul Chen: I'll draft a short tweet + status page copy. Drafting now. Who needs to approve before posting? Marketing + SRE + Legal?

Ingrid Holm: Legal only if we're naming customers or making commitments. Standard practice: comms team + SRE lead sign-off, then ops/PR as FYI. I'll review quick if it helps.

Maya Singh: I'll be on final sign-off for anything posted on our public channels. Need to ensure tone is consistent with status page and not overpromising.

Emma Carter: Plan: Paul drafts, Lia & Rajesh verify technical accuracy, Ingrid quick legal check, Maya final OK. Can we do that within the next 15-25 minutes? If yes, go ahead. Also make sure the status page entry is posted first and the tweet links to it.

Paul Chen: Draft 1 below — please comment inline.

Paul Chen: ```
Tweet draft (short):
We’re aware of increased latency affecting some API requests and are working to restore normal performance. See current status & updates: https://status.redwood.ai

Status page (short):
Investigating — We’re seeing increased API latency for a subset of requests. Our engineers have identified a cache saturation issue in the inference runtime and are applying mitigations. We will update this page as we have confirmed changes.

Customer-facing email (brief):
Subject: Notice — Temporary API latency impacting some requests
Body: Hi — We’re currently investigating increased latency affecting some API requests. Our team has identified the cause and is implementing mitigations; we do not expect data loss. We’ll send updates as we confirm recovery and any mitigations. For live status, see: https://status.redwood.ai
```

Rajesh Patel: +1 on wording. Suggest small tweak to status page first sentence: replace "a subset of requests" with "a subset of customers and routes" — more precise. Also add a note under the status page about mitigations being applied (scaling & cache refresh).

Lia Gomez: Technical note: "cache refresh" might be internal jargon. Recommend: "cache eviction and temporary autoscale" so it's clearer. Also add an ETA range if asked, but not in public text.

Paul Chen: Updated draft with those tweaks. New status page copy in code block: ```
Investigating — We’re seeing increased API latency impacting a subset of customers and routes. Our engineers have identified a cache saturation issue in the inference runtime and are applying mitigations (temporary autoscale and cache eviction). We do not expect data loss. We will post updates here as recovery is confirmed.
```

Ingrid Holm: Looks good. Two minor legal notes: (1) Don't say "we do not expect data loss" — say "we have no evidence of data loss at this time"; (2) avoid promising specific timelines.

Paul Chen: Adjusted: ```
We have no evidence of data loss at this time.
```

Maya Singh: Approving on principle. Need final thumbs from Lia or Rajesh confirming technical accuracy, then I’ll authorize posting to status and the public tweet.

Rajesh Patel: Confirmed — accurate and not misleading.

Lia Gomez: Confirmed.

Emma Carter: Final checklist before posting: 
- Status page entry posted and saved (Paul)
- Tweet drafted & scheduled/published with link to status (Paul + Maya)
- Customer email list prepared for customers with high-importance routes (Rajesh + CS team; note: don't send to everyone unless impact broad)
- Internal comms: short note in #general + incident channel with RFO to follow (Emma)

Paul Chen: Posting status page now. Will wait for Maya to greenlight tweet. 

SRE-Bot: Status page updated to "Identified" by Paul Chen at 1774500200.

Paul Chen: @Maya Singh ready for tweet sign-off. Draft below (final):
"We’re experiencing increased latency impacting a subset of customers and routes. Our engineers are applying mitigations; we have no evidence of data loss at this time. Current updates: https://status.redwood.ai"

Maya Singh: Good to go. Post it and pin the status link. Keep monitoring comments and escalate to me for press inquiries.

Paul Chen: Tweet posted and pinned. Linked to status page.

Rajesh Patel: Mitigations applied — partial recovery seen. Continuing to monitor, will update when fully recovered.

SRE-Bot: Incident update: Partial recovery observed; monitoring.

Emma Carter: Thanks team. Follow-up actions: 
- Draft an internal RFO template while we continue to observe (I'll start it).
- Prepare longer customer-facing post if recovery prolonged (Paul + Rajesh).
- Schedule brief cross-functional sync in 60m to finalize RFO.

Paul Chen: Note for social: If media picks this up, route questions to press@redwood.ai and include our status link only. Do not provide internal logs.

Ingrid Holm: Agreed. If press escalates, loop legal + comms immediately.

Emma Carter: Closing this thread — will reopen if we need new public messaging. Good job on fast alignment. :white_check_mark:
